Let \(T_P\) be the time to process one piece of part P.  
Since 5 pieces of P take the same time as 3 pieces of Q,
\[
5T_P=3T_Q \quad\Rightarrow\quad T_Q=\frac{5}{3}T_P.
\]

Let \(x\) workers process part P, so \(214-x\) process part Q.

Completion times:
\[
t_P=\frac{6000T_P}{x},\qquad
t_Q=\frac{2000T_Q}{214-x}
=\frac{2000\cdot \frac{5}{3}T_P}{214-x}
=\frac{10000T_P}{3(214-x)}.
\]

Minimize
\[
\max\left(\frac{6000}{x},\frac{10000}{3(214-x)}\right).
\]

Equal times give
\[
\frac{6000}{x}=\frac{10000}{3(214-x)}
\]
\[
18000(214-x)=10000x
\]
\[
x=\frac{963}{7}\approx 137.57.
\]

Check integers:
- \(x=137\): \(\max(6000/137,10000/(3\cdot77))\approx 43.80\)
- \(x=138\): \(\max(6000/138,10000/(3\cdot76))\approx 43.86\)

Thus the optimal integer number is \(137\).

\[
\boxed{137}
\]
